source.title: A Decade of Evidence of Trend Following Investing in Cryptocurrencies
provenance_notes: Paper identity is arXiv:2009.12155v1; exact PDF bytes remain unfrozen and reported performance is untrusted.
The accompanying public implementation is frozen in RIE-003 at commit d2e66e405183349f52556a18d387bb1dfc900db5 with exact relevant Git blob identities.

candidates.hypothesis: Systematic moving-average trend following can capture persistent cryptocurrency trends after realistic Spot execution costs.
entry_rules: Enter long when the completed-bar short moving average crosses above the completed-bar long moving average.
exit_rules: Exit to cash when the completed-bar short moving average crosses below the completed-bar long moving average; never open a short position.
stop_rules: No protective stop or target is added to this source-derived crossover search; exit is signal-driven only.
sizing_rules: Use fixed YATL research quantity 0.001 in long-only Spot research.
lookbacks: Search source-code windows n1,n2 in range(1,1000,10) hours with n1<n2 separately for SMA, EMA and DEMA.
cost_assumptions: Base search costs: 10 bps fee and 5 bps adverse slippage per execution.
Stress costs: 20 bps fee and 10 bps adverse slippage per execution.
known_limitations: The source paper studied BTCUSD Bitstamp and assumed negligible trading costs; YATL adapts to BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT Binance Spot with explicit costs.
The source forward-filled missing hourly data; YATL never fills or interpolates admitted source gaps.
Paper-reported profitability is not used as YATL evidence.
leakage_risks: All parameter and family selection must remain inside 2020-01-01 through 2023-01-01 Development data.
Blind OOS beginning 2023-01-01 cannot be read or used for selection.
Every SMA/EMA/DEMA parameter trial counts toward multiple testing.
